html:
The conversion of Kievan Rus' to Orthodox Christianity under Grand Prince Vladimir the Great of Kyiv, usually dated 988. Vladimir was baptised, and the people of Kyiv were baptised in crowds in the Dnieper.

The Russian Primary Chronicle tells that Vladimir sent envoys to compare religions, and that in Hagia Sophia they "knew not whether we were in heaven or on earth". The real bargain was political. Vladimir sent troops to help the Byzantine emperor Basil II against a revolt, and in return married the emperor's sister Anna, a rare honour.

Christianity came with Byzantine art, stone churches and the Slavonic liturgy in the Cyrillic script, already in use in Bulgaria. Monasteries such as the Kyiv Pechersk Lavra became centres of learning. Russia, Ukraine and Belarus all trace their churches to it. When the churches of Rome and Constantinople split in the schism of 1054, Rus' stayed with Constantinople, which set it apart from Catholic Poland and the West.
